title: Nick Smith: Fast Track to Production: The New Stack for Today's Founders

segments.text: Hi everybody.
I'm Nick Smith, uh, staff field engineer
at CircleCI. I've been there for a
number of years that I have stopped
counting. Um, today I'm going to show a
little bit of an odd demo because
hopefully uh if Opus 5.5 behaves, I'm
just going to hit enter here and we're
going to see CircleCI onboarding its own
project. So, a big problem with CI,
especially trying out new CI vendors,
has been that migration process. Going
from one CI to another, you have to
figure out configs, settings, all sorts
of stuff. And CircleCI recently has
updated our CLI to make it so that an
agent can do all of that for you. So all
we're going to do here is have Claude
look at a prompt that simply says fork
the express project and onboard it
within CircleCI. And we'll see that
happening here. Uh with the new CLI, you
can do anything that you could do had to
go to the UI for you can now do in the
terminal. So, not only does the agent
have access to the entire surface of
CircleCI and can crawl over it, you as
the user no longer have to go to the UI
and see all of that information. So,
with the CLI, uh, it's going to first
thing going to check to make sure that
we are authenticated. Nice thing about
our CLI is we have an OOTH
authentication method where you can set
read only, write or admin access. And we
are on the cusp of allowing you to set a
custom expiration timer for that as
well. So if you want an agent to just
look at the data in CircleCI for an
hour, that will be possible without the
agent being able to affect anything
else. So you can see right here it's
confirmed I have logged in and it's
going to start forking that project
right there. Uh and pretty soon we'll
see that starting to appear on the
pipelines page.
Uh the nice thing about uh the CLI is as
it sets up this, it's not just going to
throw some settings at CircleCI, throw a
pipeline config at CircleCI. It will be
able to see the full output of the job.
It's not just getting a status check.
It's able to see exactly what is run
inside the job, which is very, very
handy. So, it's going to go ahead and
it's asking me to fork it.
This is a new thing with the auto mode
which is fun to deal with.
Um so as it's going through and doing
that uh the other really handy features
of the cir of the CLI to help with
onboarding is we do have a way to
validate your config against uh a really
nice schema. So it lets the agent know
that it's pushing up actual config
rather than uh trying to guess at what
it sees.
So here it goes. It's going to go ahead
and create that project. And you can see
right here, uh, it is creating the
project. It's already getting a slug for
it and everything there. So we'll start
to see that pipeline coming in in a
moment. There it goes. The pipeline is
going to start being created. And the
nice thing about CircleCI pipelines is
we've actually split the pipeline up
into three different areas. Uh
traditionally a trigger comes in, a
pipeline runs and it has a set config
for that pipeline. With CircleCI we've
divided that up into three different uh
spots. The first thing you can do is you
can select where the trigger is coming
from. So repo A can trigger from repo B.
The second thing we allow you to do is
set where the code is being checked out
from. So repo A can even check out repo
B if it needs to. And then my favorite
part because I'm very uh a very big
proponent of centralizing everything is
you can select where the configuration
is coming from. So you're able to set up
a fully centralized configuration model
with CircleCI uh where you're not having
to update 500 configs every time you
need to change just a little version. So
it's gone ahead and done that first push
and we can see right there we have a
CircleCI pipeline running. uh instead of
polling the API consistently to see what
the status is. You can see right here we
have a watch command. It's not
highlighting but it's right there. That
watch command gives you a active status
live status of what the job is doing and
tells the agent what is happening inside
of it. So you can see as soon as the
build job actually finishes, which is
going to take a little longer because we
aren't caching just yet,
uh it will be able to see that green. So
as soon as we saw in the UI that green
happen, the agent saw the success happen
as well. Um so we have our first green
pipeline, but that's not typically the
best pipeline that we can do. So uh
agents typically nowadays are pretty
good at optimizing at least the first
layer of it. Uh we do provide skills
along with our CLI to help your agent
optimize for CircleCI specifically. Uh
first thing it typically does is go in
and put in some caching, but there's a
lot of other features that on CircleCI
that you can use to optimize. Uh caching
is obviously a very easy one across the
board. A newer feature of ours that can
very much help with optimization is
something called smarter testing.
So what smarter testing does is uh it
analyzes the metadata of the test suite
and will only run the tests required for
that change. So obviously if you're
dealing with a node project, some of us
have 15,000 tests that we have to run in
our unit test suite. It'd be really nice
if we only had to run 10. And that
system can make things go much much
faster whether it's for a human or an
agent.
So you can see here we are getting the
caching. It's checking on the step
timing. So we can see all the way down
to the step level exactly what's
happening in the system. There's no
guessing happening here. Um and it's
able to iterate on itself which is very
very handy.
The other nice thing about smarter
testing, uh, just to go back to that for
a second, is there's a couple other
features inside of that, I'm sure we all
have to deal with flaky tests every now
and again. And while we would all like
to fix them, we often have to do a
little bit of a band-aid. Smarter
testing allows you to rerun your tests
up to five times, so your developers
don't have to go in and manually rerun
uh, those things um, over and over and
over again. So that can definitely help
speed up uh the timeline. There
you can see we are still going in and uh
making sure that everything is installed
there. Uh we have the caching all set up
which is great. And the CLI is letting
the agent just go back and forth setting
up all the settings that it would need
to do. Um, security-wise, if you wanted
to make sure that an agent was only
setting up the configuration that you
wanted it to set up, we have a feature
called config policies, which can be
used to only allow the configuration uh
to be run that you allow. It's a reggo
policy. You can write it against the
YAML, and that makes it so that uh it
will stop a pipeline from even
triggering if there's something in the
configuration that you wouldn't allow.
and an agent can see that output with
the CLI uh and make sure to iterate
around that issue which can be very
helpful.
You it's still running here. Uh it will
go ahead and make sure that everything
is good with the lint job and it's just
iterating through. So what we did here
was take a raw project from GitHub that
had never seen CircleCI before and we're
about seven minutes in. I probably hit
it about six minutes ago and we already
have a project that's onboarded to
CircleCI. Agent can go ahead and iterate
as it goes. Uh but the actual migration
process from GitHub actions in this case
to CircleCI took about 2 minutes. So as
you're looking at CI providers and
thinking is this the best one for my
agents? Is this the best one for my
team? it is much easier to migrate do a
proof of concept and see that
information uh very quickly.
The other side just because we have a
few minutes here that I want to show off
um is we do have open telemetry and open
telemetry if you all are familiar with
it provides you a lot of information
about the system with CircleCI our open
telemetry lets you see down to the step
level. So if you have an agent that's
adds 20 extra dependencies and your
dependency install step starts bloating
on CircleCI, you would know exactly
which step uh was contributing to that
increased duration and you'd be able to
action on it. Uh this is very very
handy. My entire job is helping
customers optimize. And because we can
see down to the step level, we know if
the spin-up's taking too long, we know
if dependencies installs are taking too
long. we know if the if a bunch of
erroneous tests were added. All of that
information is very very easy to see and
this is a free feature on CircleCI. Uh
we do not charge for this whatsoever. So
end to end your agent if it was hooked
up to an open telemetry system would be
able to not only set up CircleCI
projects would also be able to optimize
those projects based on the open
telemetry data.
And I'll leave it at that.
